text: This stone weighs two and a half tons and these men have to drag it across the desert.
The Great Pyramid is made of about two point three million blocks just like it.
But dry sand piles up in front of the sled like a little wall and it gets stuck.
So one worker climbs onto the front of the sled with a jar of water.
He pours it on the sand right where the sled is headed.
The water makes tiny bridges between the grains that glue them together.
Now the sand is about twice as stiff so it stops piling up and the sled slides right over it.
In twenty fourteen scientists in Amsterdam tested this and the right amount of water cut the pull in half.
That means only about half as many men to drag the same stone.
But too much water doesn't work either so it has to be just right.
And the Egyptians knew it. A tomb painting nearly four thousand years old shows one hundred seventy two men dragging a giant statue.
And standing on the front of the sled is a man pouring water on the sand.
